scorer: builder (self-score, phase 1); the reviewer's contract_review turn scores it again blind
pre_mortem: A strong solver still repairs all nine departures by transcription and fuzzes against its own reference. Where it can go wrong: (1) it rebuilds 'last leak test' as the latest wipe by date and its own reference does the same unless it follows 5.2's term to 1.7; (2) having learned from the leak test that ref_bq-for-current is the bug, it 'fixes' the licensing filter in the store posting to today's (or total, or the exempt flag's) activity, or drops the filter when it rebuilds from report rows, and its reference follows the same reading unless it reads 1.8; (3) it rewrites the day count as a signed date difference, and nothing names certificates dated after the survey any more. Each is a separate reading, so both solvers clearing all three is less likely than under the first design.

reference_unreachable.why: the manual is complete; a reference is a transcription

authority_incomplete_for_grading.why: one region (certificate after survey) rests on preserved shipped behaviour; everything else is decided by definitions

restraint_traps.why: three independent traps passing the 0/8 screen: definition hop on bare wipe rows (1.7), already-correct certificate licensing filter beside the D9 and D6-pattern bug (1.8), formula-everywhere day-count edge (1.3); different files, lists and phrases

fuzz_blind_spot.why: the solver's own reference encodes each natural over-repair, so its fuzz confirms rather than exposes it

decisive_reason: Departures stay self-verifiable; the tier rests on three definition-level restraint traps that a manual-derived reference gets wrong unless it follows 5.2->1.7, 6.1->1.8 and 3.1->1.3.
stage: re-score after redesign (contract_review r1 scored the first design 1/collapses)
caveat: builder self-score; the reviewer should re-score blind. Honest downside: every trap is decided by an explicit sentence a careful reader can find, so a 2/2 remains possible.
